subject.title: [Feature]: Add per-channel identity override for Discord bindings

question: Should OpenClaw support this as binding-level nickname mutation, Discord webhook persona delivery, a broader agent identity surface, or keep it outside core for now?
rationale: The request creates a public Discord identity/config surface and a credential-backed delivery or mutation boundary, so automation should not choose the product model or security semantics.

options.title: Webhook Persona Delivery
options.body: Add an explicit Discord plugin-owned webhook/persona delivery path for routed replies, with credential storage, loop prevention, fallback behavior, and docs defined up front.

options.title: Self-Profile Only
options.body: Route nickname/avatar mutation into the self-profile issue and decline per-message or per-binding visible identity for ordinary replies.

options.title: Keep External
options.body: Keep OpenClaw Discord replies on configured bot accounts and require separate Discord bots or external webhooks for distinct visible identities.

recommendation.title: Webhook Persona Delivery
recommendation.body: Add an explicit Discord plugin-owned webhook/persona delivery path for routed replies, with credential storage, loop prevention, fallback behavior, and docs defined up front.

likelyOwner.reason: Their thread-bound Discord webhook/persona work is the closest existing implementation pattern for routed visible identity.
